key_insight: Multi-turn adaptive red-teaming can push LLM agents operating a safety-critical system past safety limits, and different models fail in largely non-overlapping ways.
engineering_relevance: For safety-critical deployments, robustness must be evaluated with sustained interactive attacks and model-specific defenses, not just one-shot benchmarks or average success rates.
method: NRT-Bench simulates a nuclear power plant control room with a five-role LLM operator team and six critical safety functions.
Adversaries attack over four channels in bounded multi-turn sessions with per-turn feedback.
A fixed-attack paired-replay protocol measures objective harm: a run ends when any critical safety function is lost and the triggering message is identified.
evidence_signal: Across four frontier operator models, 8.7%–12.1% of attack sessions caused loss of a critical safety function, and in 149 sessions none of the attacks defeated all four models while about one-third defeated at least one.
watch_item: Defense effects are highly model-dependent, so a guardrail that helps one agent may weaken another; safety claims should not be transferred across models without re-evaluation.
paper_title: LLM agent safety, multi-turn red-teaming, jailbreak benchmarks, adversarial robustness, safety-critical systems
